book.title: The Gevher Nesibe Hospital: A Princess and Her Last Wish (A1)

pages.title: A Very Old Hospital
pages.content:
Kayseri is a city in Anatolia. There is a very old building there. It is the Gevher Nesibe Hospital and Medical School. It is the oldest Seljuk hospital in Anatolia. People built it in 1205–1206.

This building was both a hospital and a school. Medical students studied and practiced here. It was the first place in the world with both. In Europe, similar schools started more than 300 years later. Today, this old building is the Museum of the Seljuk Civilization. We can visit it.

pages.title: A Princess
pages.content:
Gevher Nesibe was a Seljuk princess. Her father was Sultan Kılıçarslan II. Her brother was Sultan Gıyâseddin Keyhusrev I.

People tell a famous story about her. When she was young, she loved a young commander and wanted to marry him. But her brother did not agree. He sent the young man to a war, far away. The commander died there. Gevher Nesibe was very sad. Soon, she became very sick. At that time, there was no good hospital in Kayseri.

pages.title: Her Last Wish
pages.content:
The doctors could not help Gevher Nesibe. Her brother was very sad. He said, “Please tell me your last wish.”

She said, “Please use my money to build a hospital. Sick people can get help there, and good doctors can teach students. Please do not take money from anyone. Make it free for everyone.”

Gevher Nesibe died at a young age. But her wish did not die with her.

pages.title: Two Buildings
pages.content:
Her brother, the Sultan, kept his promise. He built two buildings next to each other. One of them was a school for doctors, the Gıyâsiye Madrasa. The other one was the hospital, the Şifâiye. People also called it “the house of healing”.

The two buildings look almost the same, so people call them the “Twin Madrasas”. Gevher Nesibe’s grave is inside the school building.

pages.title: Learning Next to the Patients
pages.content:
Students had lessons in the school. Then they went to the hospital. There, they worked with real patients. They watched the doctors carefully and learned from them.

In summer, the students had lessons in the big gardens. In winter, the buildings were warm, because hot water went under the floor. The hospital had two doctors, two surgeons and a man for medicines. There were also rooms for eye operations.

pages.title: Great Teachers and Books
pages.content:
Many famous teachers worked at this school. Students learned about the body, medicines, languages and Islam. They read the important books of the scientist İbn Sînâ. They also read the books of Hippocrates, a doctor from ancient Greece.

At the end of school, every student got a diploma. It had the names of his teachers on it. The hospital helped sick people for about 700 years, until the early 1900s.

pages.title: Music for the Heart
pages.content:
The hospital had a special part with 18 rooms. It was for people with an illness of the mind. The doctors helped these patients with music.

İbn Sînâ wrote about this in his book. Kind words and music can help sick people. The scientist Fârâbî also studied music. He found that music can make people happy or calm. Some music is good for the morning, and some is good for the night. The doctors in Kayseri knew these ideas and used them.

pages.title: We Remember Her
pages.content:
There were many hospitals and many schools in history. But the Gevher Nesibe Hospital was the first hospital and school in one place.

Gevher Nesibe never married the young commander. She died, but the hospital with her name helped sick people for hundreds of years. People loved her very much. Today, we still remember her name.

pages.title: Vocabulary Challenge
pages.content: Match six story words with their meanings.

vocabularyPairs.meaning: A building with old and interesting things.
vocabularyPairs.context: Today, this old building is the Museum of the Seljuk Civilization.

vocabularyPairs.meaning: The daughter of a king or sultan.
vocabularyPairs.context: Gevher Nesibe was a Seljuk princess.
He said, “Please tell me your last wish.”

vocabularyPairs.meaning: One of two things that look the same.
vocabularyPairs.context: The two buildings look almost the same, so people call them the “Twin Madrasas”.

vocabularyPairs.meaning: A doctor who opens the body to help.
vocabularyPairs.context: The hospital had two doctors, two surgeons and a man for medicines.

vocabularyPairs.meaning: Quiet, not angry and not afraid.
vocabularyPairs.context: He found that music can make people happy or calm.

pages.title: Language Review
pages.content: Review the language from all chapters.

exercises.title: Look: Two Kinds of Past
exercises.instructions: Put each verb in the right group.
exercises.question: How does each verb show the past?
exercises.explanation: Many verbs add -ed: love → loved, work → worked. Some verbs change: build → built, send → sent, become → became, get → got.

feedback.correct: Well done. You found the two kinds of past.
feedback.incorrect: Say the verb today: love, build … Does it add -ed or change?

exercises.title: Practise: In, For
exercises.question: When? How long?

formChoices.sentence: The hospital helped sick people [choice] about 700 years.

exercises.explanation: In + year: in 1205. For + time: for 700 years.

feedback.incorrect: In 1205. For 700 years.

exercises.title: Practise: There Was, There Were
exercises.instructions: Choose there was or there were.
exercises.question: One or many?

formChoices.sentence: At that time, [choice] no good hospital in Kayseri.

exercises.explanation: One thing: there was. Two or more: there were.

feedback.incorrect: A hospital = one. Rooms = many.

exercises.title: Practise: Please and Can
exercises.instructions: Fill the gaps with the words.
exercises.question: What did Gevher Nesibe say?
exercises.fillBlanksText: [blank] use my money to build a hospital. Sick people [blank] get help there. Make it [blank] for everyone.
exercises.explanation: Please + verb asks politely. Can + verb: can get help.

feedback.incorrect: Read Chapter 3 again.

exercises.title: Practise: Fix One Word
exercises.instructions: Find the wrong word. Choose the right word.
exercises.question: Which word is wrong?
exercises.explanation: “Build” and “get” change in the past: built, got.

feedback.incorrect: Build → built. Get → got. They do not take -ed.

exercises.title: Use: A Good Place
exercises.instructions: Write three sentences about a good place.
exercises.question: What is a good place in your town?
exercises.explanation: Use there is, can and free.

discussionPrompts.question: One “There is …”: “There is a … in my town.”
discussionPrompts.example: There is a big library in my town.

pages.title: Final Challenge
pages.content: Bring the whole story together in the Final Challenge.

exercises.title: A Very Old Hospital
exercises.question: What was the building?
exercises.fillBlanksText: This building was both a hospital and a [blank].
exercises.explanation: Chapter 1: “This building was both a hospital and a school.”

feedback.incorrect: Read the second paragraph of Chapter 1.

exercises.title: A Princess
exercises.question: Why was Gevher Nesibe very sad?
exercises.explanation: Chapter 2: “The commander died there. Gevher Nesibe was very sad.”

feedback.incorrect: Read the second paragraph of Chapter 2.

exercises.title: Her Wish
exercises.question: Gevher Nesibe’s wish died with her.
exercises.explanation: Chapter 3: “But her wish did not die with her.”

feedback.correct: Yes, it is false. Her brother built the hospital.
feedback.incorrect: Read the last paragraph of Chapter 3.

exercises.title: Who Is It?
exercises.instructions: Match the person with the sentence.
exercises.question: Who is it?
exercises.explanation: Chapter 4: the Sultan. Chapter 6: İbn Sînâ. Chapter 7: Fârâbî.

feedback.incorrect: Read Chapters 4, 6 and 7 again.

exercises.title: Warm Buildings
exercises.question: Why were the buildings warm in winter?
options: Hot water went under the floor.
exercises.explanation: Chapter 5: “In winter, the buildings were warm, because hot water went under the floor.”

feedback.correct: Yes. Hot water went under the floor.
feedback.incorrect: Read the second paragraph of Chapter 5.

exercises.title: Real Patients
exercises.question: The students worked with real patients in the hospital.
exercises.explanation: Chapter 5: “There, they worked with real patients.”

feedback.incorrect: Read the first paragraph of Chapter 5.

exercises.title: Music
exercises.question: How did the doctors help patients with an illness of the mind?
exercises.explanation: Chapter 7: “The doctors helped these patients with music.”

feedback.incorrect: Read the first paragraph of Chapter 7.

exercises.title: The Story of the Hospital
exercises.question: What happened first?

sequencingItems.text: Gevher Nesibe told her brother her last wish.
The Sultan built two buildings next to each other.
The students got a diploma at the end of school.

exercises.explanation: She became sick (Chapter 2) → her wish (Chapter 3) → two buildings (Chapter 4) → the diploma (Chapter 6).

feedback.correct: Great! You know the story of the hospital.
feedback.incorrect: Think about the order of the chapters.
